gap: No result ChatGPT got states the only named hands-on figures for a 100-key Lofree low-profile board: PCWorld's Mattias Inghe (published 2026-09-23) rated the Flow 2 100 3 out of 5, listed it at 870 g and 39.8 x 12.6 x 2.15 cm, and saw the battery drop 20% in three days on Bluetooth; nor that RTINGS tested the number-pad size itself for only the Keychron K5 Max, Logitech MX Mechanical and Logitech G915 X LIGHTSPEED, and the 75% sibling for the Lofree Flow100 and NuPhy Air100 V3.
standout_why: Compared against RTINGS' best low-profile list (updated 2026-10-09) and its K5 Max, G915 X LIGHTSPEED, MX Mechanical, Flow84/Flow100 and Air75 V3 reviews. RTINGS holds the deciding lab numbers (latency, height, weight, travel, noise), but every one showed as 'Locked' behind membership when I read the pages on 2026-11-26, so I could not collect them side by side. The RTINGS pages already state which variant was tested; what they lack is any number for a Lofree number-pad board, which PCWorld and Notebookcheck supply. Technobezz returned HTTP 403 and was not read; purchase.fyi, keebscout, Tom's Guide and Tom's Hardware were not opened.
decides: It confirms the Keychron K5 Max as the pick with the strongest independent testing: RTINGS bought the full-size unit itself and names it Best Low-Profile Keyboard For Gaming. It does not lift a Lofree row. The Flow100 has no 2.4 GHz and RTINGS calls its wireless performance 'exceptionally poor' (tested on the Flow84); the Flow 2 100 got 3/5 from PCWorld for a cramped number pad; the Flow Lite 2 100 has no named measurement at all. On this angle a Lofree board can place only on price and stock, not on measurements.

findings.label: RTINGS measurements locked to non-members
findings.value: Height, width, depth, weight, single-key and multi-key latency, USB polling rate, average loudness, pre-travel, total travel and actuation force all show 'Locked' on the K5 Max, G915 X LIGHTSPEED, MX Mechanical, Flow84/Flow100 and Air75 V3 reviews
findings.source_title: Keychron K5 Max [K1 Max, K3 Max, etc.] Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Direct fetch returned only site navigation, so all RTINGS pages were read through the r.jina.ai text reader of the same URLs. The K5 Max vs NuPhy Air75 V2 compare table (https://www.rtings.com/keyboard/tools/compare/keychron-k5-max-k1-max-k3-max-etc-nuphy-air75-v2-air60-v2-air96-v2/49533/42068) shows the same fields Locked.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS bought and tested
findings.value: Full-size (100%) K5 Max, RGB backlight, Gateron Low Profile 2.0 Mechanical Red switches
findings.source_title: Keychron K5 Max [K1 Max, K3 Max, etc.] Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS: 'We bought and tested the full-size K5 Max model with Gateron Low Profile 2.0 Mechanical Red switches.' Converted to Test Bench 1.4.3 on 2026-03-17. The compare table lists the tested unit's 'Hot-Swappable Switches' as 'No'.

findings.label: RTINGS pick category and polling rate
findings.value: Best Low-Profile Keyboard For Gaming; 1,000 Hz wired or on the 2.4 GHz receiver
findings.source_title: The 5 Best Low-Profile Keyboards - Black Friday 2026 - RTINGS.com
findings.note: List updated 2026-10-09. RTINGS: 'support a 1000Hz polling rate when used wired or through the included 2.4GHz USB receiver'. It is the only mechanical board with a number pad among the five picks; the others are the NuPhy Air75 V3 (no numpad) and three scissor-switch boards.

findings.label: Maximum switch travel, as RTINGS states it
findings.value: 3.0 mm, against 3.5 mm for the Gateron Low-Profile 3.0 switches on the NuPhy Air V3 series
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 [Air65 V3, Air100 V3] Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS comparison text: the NuPhy switches 'provide a full 3.5 mm of travel, which is longer than the Keychron's maximum of 3.0 mm.' This is the only travel figure visible without membership.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS tested
findings.value: The 75% Air75 V3 (Nebula Dark, Gateron Nano Blush switches), not the Air100 V3
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 [Air65 V3, Air100 V3] Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS: 'We expect all our test results to apply to each size variant'. Air100 V3 information was added 2026-04-22, after the original review. RTINGS credits the series with a 1,000 Hz polling rate and 'very good latency'; the ms figures are Locked.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS tested and its wireless verdict
findings.value: Tested the 75% Flow84; Flow100 described as 'a larger variant with a 96% form factor'. Cons: 'No 2.4GHz connectivity', 'Exceptionally poor wireless performance'
findings.note: Review published 2025-06-19, updated 2026-01-06. RTINGS: 'they only support Bluetooth connectivity, which has dramatically higher latency that you will notice in-game'. It also says 'the larger Flow100 is ideal if you need a numpad for the work you do'. RTINGS calls it 96%, so it sits just under a strict 104-key full size.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS tested
findings.note: Converted to Test Bench 1.4.3 on 2026-01-22, last updated 2026-02-05. Wired latency shows 'N/A'; every other measurement is Locked. RTINGS' K5 Max page notes the MX Mechanical 'has keycaps with shine-through legends'.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS tested
findings.source_title: Logitech G915 X LIGHTSPEED Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS: 'We bought and tested a White color model with Tactile switches.' It counts nine dedicated macro keys and a full set of media controls. Every measurement is Locked.

findings.label: PCWorld hands-on: rating, size, weight
findings.value: 3 out of 5; 39.8 x 12.6 x 2.15 cm; 870 g; $169 at Lofree
findings.note: By Mattias Inghe of PC för Alla, translated from Swedish; tested August 2026 with the Nordic layout, published 2026-09-23. The page does not say whether the reviewer weighed the board or took the figures from the maker. PCWorld: 'the numeric keypad on the right is squeezed tightly next to the Enter and arrow keys'; a 3 cm strip right of the number pad adds width.

findings.label: PCWorld battery observation
findings.value: Battery dropped 20% over three days, on Bluetooth only (not the 2.4 GHz adapter); 3,000 mAh
findings.note: Reviewer's own use, not a timed rundown; backlight level not stated. Lofree's claim, as PCWorld quotes it, is about 120 hours of use or up to 14 hours at maximum backlight.

findings.label: Notebookcheck battery estimates on the 84-key sibling
findings.value: About 100 h on Bluetooth with no backlight; 16.6 h on Bluetooth at maximum backlight; about 10 h on 2.4 GHz at maximum backlight (2,000 mAh)
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow Lite mechanical keyboard review: Excellent low-profile design just misses glory (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: By Julian van der Merwe, published 2025-02-01, updated 2026-10-05. Tested the Flow Lite84, not the Lite100, which appears only as a $109 price point. Notebookcheck: 'These battery life results are estimates based on monitoring the battery drain over the course of a few work days'. Its spec table gives 1,000 Hz on USB-C and 2.4 GHz and 125 Hz on Bluetooth.

findings.label: RTINGS notable mention
findings.value: 'ultra-low-profile switches have very short travel'; costs considerably more than the K5 Max
findings.source_title: The 5 Best Low-Profile Keyboards - Black Friday 2026 - RTINGS.com
findings.note: No mm figure is given on the list page. The Logitech MX Mechanical and G915 X do not appear on this list at all.
